features.overlay: Caret inserts 'an array with at least one entry, exactly one of which is' into the UR3 signature's /Reference description, before the signature-reference dictionary carrying the UR transform. This is on Table 263, not Table 264.
features.status: producer constraint on the Reference array and UR transform cardinality
features.consumer_assertions: pdf-signature/src/signature.rs::permissions routes the UR3 signature to usage_rights; usage_rights iterates /Reference entries and uses the first recognized UR/UR3 transform. viewer-core/src/notes.rs uses the resulting rights in an open-time statement and in Table 258 revision comparison. Current signature/revision assertions use one valid UR transform; none challenges multiplicity. Table 264 legal_information does not inspect this field.
features.verdict: Correct the prior signatures_transforms erratum locator: #218 is Table 263, not Table 264. The source wording constrains producer shape; this review does not infer a mandatory reader rejection or rights policy for a malformed multi-UR signature, so no failing test is proposed. The parser behavior is observable in permission reporting/comparison but its treatment of a nonconforming multi-UR array remains a reader-policy boundary, not a confirmed conformance defect.
features.prior_review: signatures_transforms currently misattributes #218 to Table 264; owner should correct that entry. Relevant permission consumer is in signature_framing_current/signatures_transforms and viewer-core/src/notes.rs.

features.clause: 12.10.2 Table 269 PCSM; §14.11.7 Table 407 OPI Inks value description
features.overlay: Two StrikeOuts remove 'real': one from the PCSM matrix value description and one from the OPI Inks tint description. The latter is visibly the word 'real' in 'real number' in the Table 407 Inks row; the former has its own distinct table target.
features.status: numeric type wording corrections; PDF number objects include integer and real representations
features.consumer_assertions: measurement_geospatial_current already covers the PCSM path with numeric arrays and asymmetric transform controls. Repository archive rules inspect OPI-key presence for PDF/A restrictions, not OPI Inks tint metadata; no OPI interpretation consumer was found.
features.verdict: The PCSM behavior is already covered and the correction does not change the affine algorithm. No unsupported claim of full OPI metadata parsing; no new test warranted absent an OPI consumer.
